claim: A single-pass, attention-weighted probe over LLM hidden states (AutoProbe) achieves only 0.63-0.77 accuracy predicting functional correctness of independent-unit code across six open code LLMs, far below the near-perfect calibration achievable via repeated sampling.
stance_target: internal representations encode meaningful correctness signal, but single-pass hidden-state probes do not close the gap to expensive n-sample AUROC
scope_conditions: HumanEval/MBPP-style independent-unit Python code; DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B/6.7B, CodeLlama-7B/13B, Magicoder-7B, CodeGemma-7B
quoted_support: AutoProbe reaches an F1-Score of 0.76... In the independent-unit setting, generated code snippets are often short and simple, offering limited discriminative signals.

claim: Even an exhaustive Oracle baseline that searches all layer/token combinations per model only reaches 0.66-0.77 accuracy on independent-unit functionality assessment, suggesting a ceiling on single-forward-pass hidden-state signal, not merely a probe-design limitation.
stance_target: the internal->expressed gap may reflect a genuine informational ceiling for single-pass representations on simple/short code, not just insufficient probe architecture
scope_conditions: independent-unit HumanEval/MBPP/DevEval-style code; six open code LLMs
quoted_support: Oracle represents an upper-bound baseline constructed by exhaustively searching across all layers and token positions to identify the most optimal internal representations of each model for each evaluation setting.
numbers: Oracle accuracy 0.66-0.77 across six models on independent-unit functionality

claim: External LLM-as-Judge (verbalized confidence via a separate model, o4-mini) outperforms all representation-based probes on independent-unit functional-correctness assessment, averaging 0.94 accuracy, but its performance collapses to 0.70-0.80 on repo-level multi-file code.
stance_target: the claim that no expressed interface communicates code correctness signal well -- verbalized LLM-as-judge is highly effective for simple, self-contained functions
scope_conditions: independent-unit vs repo-level code; DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama, Magicoder, CodeGemma families
quoted_support: External LLM-AJ achieves an average accuracy of 0.94, exceeding that of the other approaches by 32-121%... these scores significantly drop to... 0.80 when assessing the correctness of repo-level code.
numbers: up to 0.97 accuracy on CodeLlama-7B independent-unit

claim: On repo-level (multi-file) code, representation-based probes (AutoProbe) outperform verbalized LLM-as-judge and approach or exceed the Oracle, reversing the pattern seen on independent-unit code.
stance_target: which expressed interface works best is context-dependent (code complexity/length), complicating a single blanket claim about internal vs expressed signal quality
quoted_support: AutoProbe reaches an average accuracy of 0.82, which is comparable to the Oracle's performance and surpasses the other approaches by up to 111%.
numbers: improvement up to 111% over some baselines

claim: AutoProbe's hidden-state extraction and inference add essentially zero cost: extraction is concurrent with the single generation pass (no added latency) and classifier inference takes 0.6 milliseconds per code unit, versus 83 minutes to train black-box embedding-based baselines (CodeBERT/CodeT5+).
stance_target: single-pass internal probing is a genuinely cheap candidate expressed-uncertainty interface (feasible on single-GPU 7B setups)
scope_conditions: NVIDIA A6000 48GB GPU, six code LLMs up to 13B parameters
quoted_support: the training phase requires just about 1 minute, and the inference phase takes only 0.6 milliseconds per generated code unit... the extraction was performed concurrently during code generation and did not introduce additional latency into the generation process.
numbers: extraction ~125 hours for entire dataset (concurrent with generation)

claim: Prior white-box SOTA (Openia) fails when correctness signal is not consistently located at the same layer/token position across model architectures -- correctness-related internal representations are highly model-dependent in location.
stance_target: internal correctness signals exist but their location within the network is architecture-specific, motivating dynamic/adaptive probing over fixed-position probing
scope_conditions: DeepSeek Coder, Code Llama, Magicoder compared on identical near-duplicate incorrect generations
quoted_support: Despite the nearly identical functions, Openia yields inconsistent predictions about their functional correctness... This inconsistency arises because Openia relies on the fixed representation of only the last generated token... at the final layer of the models.
numbers: Magicoder F1 improves from 0.42 at first layer to 0.69 at final layer (40% relative gain, last-token)

claim: For security-vulnerability assessment, AutoProbe (a single-pass probe) beats the SOTA white-box baseline Openia by up to 18% and both In-house and External LLM-as-Judge by 24-133% and 19-82% respectively, showing internal probing is markedly stronger than verbalized judgment for security correctness specifically.
stance_target: task type (security vs functionality) determines which expressed interface (probe vs verbalized) is more effective, so a one-size-fits-all interface claim is too coarse
scope_conditions: SecurityEval, CWEval, CODEGUARD+, SALLM benchmarks, six code LLMs
quoted_support: Compared to the white-box approach Openia, AutoProbe yields improvement gains of up to 18%... The accuracy of In-house LLM-AJ lags behind AutoProbe by margins ranging from 24% to 133%.
numbers: AutoProbe accuracy 0.82-0.91 across models for security
